newsitem.title: USA: Bristol-Myers, Research Triangle in pact.
newsitem.headline: Bristol-Myers, Research Triangle in pact.

text.p: Bristol-Myers Squibb Co said on Wednesday it formed a research and licensing pact with the Research Triangle Institute to develop synthetic third-generation analogs of naturally occurring plant alkaloids with cancer-fighting properties.

Research Triangle Institute is an independent non-profit organization that conducts research for government and industry in the fields of health, medicine, environmental protection, advanced technology and public policy.
Bristol said it believed analogs of the compounds, which were known as camptothecins, had the potential to become effective chemotherapeutic agents.

Under terms of the deal, Bristol said it would fund a three-year research program at Research Triangle to provide the pharmaceutical company with camptothecin analogs for late- stage preclinical testing and development.
Research Triangle would receive additional funds that partly support its research operations, Bristol said.
The camptothecin compounds covered in the agreement are third-generation synthetic analogs of a chemical found in a tree native to China, the company said.
